text: Anant Gangaram Geete, born on 2 June 1951, is an Indian politician who served as the Union Cabinet Minister for Heavy Industries and Public Sector Enterprises from 2014 to 2019 in the Narendra Modi cabinet. He previously held the position of Union Cabinet Minister for Power from August 2002 to May 2004. He is a member of the Shiv Sena (Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray) political party in Maharashtra, India. Geete has been elected to the Lok Sabha six times. In the 2009 general election, he won from the Raigad constituency by a margin of 145,000 votes, defeating the then sitting MP and former Cabinet Minister A.R. Antulay. In the 2014 election, he retained his seat in Raigad by a margin of 2,110 votes over Sunil Tatkare, who was then the Minister for Water Resources in Maharashtra; however, Tatkare lost the seat in 2019 by a margin of 31,740 votes. Prior to Raigad, he represented the Ratnagiri constituency for four terms, from the 11th to the 14th Lok Sabha. He was born in Tisangi, a village in Ratnagiri District, Maharashtra. Geete has held several key positions, including Chief Whip of the Shiv Sena Parliamentary party, Member of the Consultative Committee of the Ministry of Human Resource Development, Leader of the Shiv Sena Parliamentary Party, Member of the General Purposes Committee, Member of the Railway Convention Committee, Chairman of the Committee on Chemicals and Fertilizers, Member of the Committee on Petitions, Leader of the Shiv Sena Parliamentary Party in the Lok Sabha, and Member of the Committee on Food, Consumer Affairs & Public Distribution and the Business Advisory Committee.
